abstract: Wang, Wei and Wang (Purdue) build a dynamic, posting-level measure of generative-AI exposure from 9.4 million Lightcast US job postings (January 2021–June 2025), using a two-stage LLM pipeline that extracts tasks from each posting and classifies whether current GenAI can substantially cut the time needed for each one. Mean exposure is not fixed: it rises to a peak of 0.415 in early 2022, falls to a trough of 0.378 through 2023, then partly recovers. A three-fold Kitagawa decomposition splits the post-Q3-2023 decline into hiring reallocation across occupation-industry-seniority cells (52%), within-cell job redesign (39.5%) and their interaction (8.5%). A complementary Oaxaca–Blinder decomposition finds that occupational shifts explain about 90% of the exposure change attributable to observable job characteristics. Adjustment differs by seniority: senior postings adjust earlier and mainly through reallocation (70.8% of their contribution), while junior postings adjust through reallocation (60.15%), redesign (18.22%) and a large interaction term (21.63%). The authors read this as firms reorganizing both where they hire and what jobs contain, not simply cutting exposed jobs.
keyFindings: Mean posting-level GenAI exposure (β index, 0–1) peaked at 0.415 in early 2022 and fell to 0.378 during 2023 before partly recovering
From Q3 2023, hiring reallocation explains 52% of the decline in aggregate exposure, within-job redesign 39.46% and their interaction 8.54%
Occupational shifts account for about 90% of the exposure change explained by observable job characteristics (Oaxaca–Blinder)
Junior postings: reallocation 60.15%, redesign 18.22%, interaction 21.63% of the aggregate absolute contribution from Q3 2023
Senior postings adjust earlier and mainly through reallocation (70.80%); senior exposure fell from 0.595 to 0.571 pre- to post-GPT
Seniority gradient: mean β of 0.582 for senior, 0.426 for junior and 0.381 for intermediate postings
methodology: Lightcast universe of US online job postings, all sectors, January 2021–June 2025 (188M+ raw postings); repeated random sampling within occupation × seniority × industry cells yields 9,373,092 postings. Two-stage LLM pipeline: task extraction and matching to skill groups, then task-level classification of direct/indirect GenAI exposure (Eloundou-style rubric), aggregated to posting-level indices α, β (main) and γ. Validated against a replication of Eloundou et al. (2024) occupation-level exposure. Three-fold Kitagawa decomposition (composition, within-cell, interaction) and weighted Oaxaca–Blinder pre/post-GPT decomposition; heterogeneity by Lightcast seniority (junior, intermediate, senior).
qualifiers: Tier 2: unrefereed arXiv working paper. Exposure is an LLM-classified index of posting text, not observed AI use or employment outcomes. Decomposition shares describe a change in an index, not job losses or wage changes; the paper makes no causal claim about employment. Postings text may change for reasons other than AI (writing conventions, the LLM classifier, Lightcast parsing). Seniority labels come from job titles and posting text. The Q3-2023 break is interpreted, not identified, as the move from experimentation to enterprise deployment.
